# Allium $40m Series B Powers Push for Institutional Blockchain Data Standardization

Allium $40m Series B funding marks a key moment as institutions seek standardized onchain data infrastructure. Allium, a blockchain data platform serving enterprises and financial institutions, has closed a $40 million Series B funding round as demand grows for reliable blockchain data solutions. The round was led by Amplify Partners, with existing investors Kleiner Perkins and Theory Ventures participating. As part of the deal, Amplify's David Beyer will join Allium's board. The company has now raised over $60 million total, building on its $16.5 million Series A in 2024. [Source 1](https://fintech.global/2026/06/24/why-alliums-40m-raise-could-reshape-onchain-finance/) [Source 2](https://www.fintechfutures.com/venture-capital-funding/allium-bags-40m-to-accelerate-blockchain-data-analysis-offering)

The timing matters. Stablecoin circulation has reached $302 billion, onchain payments volume hit $394 billion in 2025, and tokenized financial instruments now account for $27.6 billion. Despite this growth, institutions have lacked a reliable, standardized way to operate within these systems at scale.

## Scaling Enterprise Clients and Market Reach

Since its Series A, Allium has grown revenue more than tenfold and now serves over 150 enterprise clients spanning financial institutions, fintech companies, and government agencies. Among its notable partnerships, Visa worked with Allium's data to build its Onchain Analytics Dashboard, giving partners live visibility into onchain payment flows and wider ecosystem activity. BCG also relies on the platform to underpin stablecoin payments research and digital asset advisory services for institutional clients.

### Enterprise Adoption Drivers

Several factors are driving institutional adoption of blockchain data platforms. First, regulatory scrutiny requires accurate onchain data for compliance and reporting. Second, portfolio allocation to digital assets demands better analytics. Third, client demand for crypto-native products forces traditional institutions to build onchain capabilities. Allium positions itself as the infrastructure layer that feeds these workflows.

### Notable Client Partnerships

Visa's collaboration with Allium stands out as a validation of the platform's enterprise readiness. The Onchain Analytics Dashboard provides Visa partners with real-time visibility into payment flows and ecosystem activity. Meanwhile, BCG's use of Allium data for stablecoin research underscores how traditional consulting firms are building crypto advisory practices. These partnerships signal broader institutional acceptance of blockchain data as a legitimate asset class.

The platform addresses a persistent challenge in the blockchain sector. Data fragmentation across chains makes it difficult for institutions to get a coherent picture of onchain activity. Allium standardizes and enriches information across more than 150 blockchain networks, and its data has been cited by authoritative bodies including the Federal Reserve and Stanford.

## Product Suite and AI Opportunity

Allium's flagship product, Terminal, delivers analytics through dashboards, APIs, and data warehouse integrations, enabling trading, compliance, and product workflows. Rather than limiting data to visualization, the platform allows users to track where growth is occurring, monitor how stablecoins and tokenized assets are being deployed, and feed insights directly into broader organizational workflows.

### Terminal Capabilities

Terminal serves multiple use cases. Traders use it for real-time market intelligence and portfolio tracking. Compliance teams leverage it for transaction monitoring and suspicious activity detection. Product teams integrate its data into wallet applications, trading platforms, and custodian systems. This multi-function approach differentiates Allium from point solutions that serve only one workflow.

### AI and Agentic Commerce

Looking ahead, Allium sees opportunity in the rise of AI-driven and agentic systems conducting commerce onchain. As autonomous agents begin using stablecoins to make purchases and move funds across blockchain networks, demand for robust, finance-grade data infrastructure is expected to intensify. The company is already positioning its platform to handle machine-readable financial data at scale.

Allium co-founder and CEO Ethan Chan said, "Every major financial workflow runs on a system of record. Whether it's Bloomberg for market data, DTCC for securities settlement, or SWIFT for payment messaging, these systems underpin how global finance operates. As finance moves onchain, there's still no shared, institutional-grade system of record, leaving institutions operating at scale without a reliable source of truth. We're building the foundation that brings institutional-grade reliability and standardization to onchain finance."

## Conclusion

Allium's $40 million Series B underscores the growing demand for standardized blockchain data infrastructure among institutions. With over 150 clients including major names like Visa and BCG, the company is positioning itself as the missing system of record for onchain finance. As stablecoins, tokenized assets, and AI-driven agents increasingly move financial activity onto blockchain networks, platforms like Allium that deliver reliable, standardized data at scale will become essential infrastructure for the next phase of institutional crypto adoption.

Allium is a blockchain data platform that aggregates and standardizes information across more than 150 blockchain networks, serving enterprise clients including financial institutions, fintech companies, and government agencies.

Allium serves over 150 enterprise clients. Notable partnerships include Visa, which used Allium's data for its Onchain Analytics Dashboard, and BCG, which relies on the platform for stablecoin payments research and digital asset advisory services.

**4. Why is institutional blockchain data important?**

Institutions need reliable, standardized data to operate effectively onchain. Fragmentation across chains has historically made it difficult for financial institutions to understand and participate in blockchain-based finance at scale. Platforms like Allium provide the infrastructure needed for trading, compliance, and product decisions.

**5. What is Allium's growth trajectory?**

Since its Series A in 2024, Allium has grown revenue more than tenfold. The company has raised over $60 million total funding and is currently hiring across engineering, product, and go-to-market roles.
